questions.prompt: Which keyword starts a conditional block?
questions.explanation: The if keyword is used to test a condition and execute code when it is true.
The syntax is if (condition). The condition must evaluate to a bool.

questions.prompt: What keyword provides an alternative block when the if is false?
questions.explanation: The else keyword runs when the if condition evaluates to false.
The if block and else block must each be enclosed in braces when containing multiple statements.

questions.prompt: What keyword allows additional conditions after an if?
questions.explanation: else if adds another condition to test when the previous if or else if was false.

questions.prompt: In a ternary operator, what separates the true and false results?
questions.explanation: The ternary operator uses ? for the true branch and : for the false branch.

questions.prompt: Which form is more concise: if-else or ternary?
questions.explanation: The ternary operator is a shorthand for simple if-else assignments.

questions.prompt: What happens if no condition in an if-else if chain is true?
options: The else block runs if present
questions.explanation: If none of the conditions are true, the else block executes. If there is no else, nothing runs.
